superficial: An enormous metal ring over a pit and, at its center, a closed and silent core with the old motor inside. Around it, a console and an empty cradle: everything is ready to receive something that never arrived.
On the ring, a plate: “Engine Room. The Counterweight is fitted here.”
profunda: Now I understand the mechanism: the core beats, and it opens only during the pulse. One motor goes in as the other comes out, in the same beat.
Between beats, the core is shut, and whoever tries to open it out of time only wastes strength.

superficial: Dozens of cuts in the ground and the walls, all spherical and perfect, as if something had bitten the world. The edges are smooth and curved.
Every Gate that was opened left one nearby. There are recent cuts and old ones, one inside another.
profunda: In one of the bites there is a carved wall with half a symbol: two rings split by a broken line. It is the half that my fragment lacks: they fit, edge to edge.
The fragments at home came from here.

superficial: A recorder on the desk of the post. When you press it, a voice drags every syllable as if speaking from the bottom of a well.
profunda: If you understand me, you have turned the wheel far enough. Where I record, one of your days is five.
I record inside the Knot, on the inner face, with the seed hanging overhead.
From outside you will not see us where we are: the light that leaves here bends toward the Ember.
To find us, look at the image and turn your gaze away from the Ember by about eighteen degrees.
The Council will say there is no risk. There is a Limit, and every trip brings us closer to it.

superficial: The machine’s log: a paper tape with a line that rises and falls. Every use of a Gate leaves a spike; the spikes, small at first, gradually bunch together.
Toward the end the line shoots up. Someone wrote in the margin, in a hurry: “During the evacuation they were all used at once. The faster they ran, the higher it went.”
profunda: I know which evacuation it means: forty minutes, Gates 2 to 6. On the tape it is a single enormous spike.
The last entries are in another hand, calmer: “A new call has been logged. A young mouth, in a system we do not yet know, is looking for us.”
And below: “The core only opens during the pulse. That is where the Counterweight will go, if it arrives.”

superficial: The list of worlds connected to the network, on a wall of plates. Each line has a name and an hour written beside it; between them there are gaps.
The hours do not add up: one and the same Gate shows a different hour at each mouth. Someone has scratched “does not add up” and written it again on every row.
profunda: In one of the gaps a symbol is carved: two rings with a line down the middle. It is the same one that split my fragment, and someone has filled in the gap.
My system is already on the network.

superficial: The ruins of an enormous ring, the first one, half fallen. The plaza around it is full of tools left in order, as if for coming back.
In the center of the ring there is no empty air: there is a point where the sight bends, like a scar.
profunda: With what I know about the dark point in the sky, I look at this mouth differently: it did not close properly. What was left when it closed badly is the thing that bends light up there.
The Knot was born here.

superficial: A cliff facing the sky: the edge of the world. From here you see the whole sky and, in it, a dark point ringed by bent stars, as if stretched.
It is enormously heavy: light bends around it. On the railing someone carved a name: “the Knot.” Toward the end of the cycle it seems blacker and bigger.
profunda: With what I know about the Slow Site, I see the bent stars in another way: the light that leaves from near the Knot bends the same.
Whatever hides beside the dark point I will see where it is not.

superficial: A thick lever on the console in front of the core, with a plate: “Extractor. Pull only before the pulse.”
A cable joins it to the core. When it is pulled, something big moves inside and the old motor rises through the opening until it is out.
Without the old motor the core waits for another: the lever is for that, not for stopping the machine.

A metal cradle in front of the core, made to fit something the size of a barrel. On one side, two wheels, one for minutes and one for seconds; on the other, the machine’s clock, and next to it a gap for the clock of whatever is placed in the cradle.
The wheels turn with a firm click, as if they had been made so as not to go wrong in a hurry.
profunda: Now I understand: whatever is placed here carries its own clock, and it only fits if it shows the same as the machine’s. To match them, the wheels are turned.
It is what the note at the Workshop said: it must not be moved without adjusting the clock.

superficial: Beneath the plaza of the First Gate, a vault. On the floor, a plug of clamped rings; on the back wall, an inscription.
profunda: “Here the first throat opened. We could not close it: we folded it over itself and sent it far away, where its weight would not reach us.”
“Let no one lift this seal. What lies beneath is no longer here, but it still pulls.”

superficial: A long relief on the inner face: small figures carrying rock out of the centre and taking it, in rings, upward.
profunda: The frieze goes on: every forged ring is a Gate, and every opened Gate leaves a bite in the shell.
At the end, the figures look at the hollow they have made. One points to the centre, where no rock is left.

superficial: From the band's viewer you can see the centre: a black point, small as a seed, with a ring of light that bends whatever lies behind it.
profunda: It is the same as the Knot, but tiny and awake. The machine surrounds it so it will not grow; with every pulse, the ring of light widens a little.

superficial: A departures board on the inner face. Destinations, times, Gate numbers. Almost all crossed out.
profunda: The last lines are handwritten, more crooked each time. The very last one has no destination: only a time, and no one crossed it out.

superficial: At the foot of the Beacon, a plaque: “Passage signal. Keep ships away from the dust.”
profunda: Below, another hand added: “All of this was ground. What the Gates bit off and did not take stayed here, turning. The rest fell into other skies.”
